mainTopic: How a partly released נדר works according to רבה and רבא: the listed-people משנה, the onion משנה, and רבי נתן's challenge.
overview: This amud continues the argument between רבה and רבא about a נדר that is partly released. רבא is challenged: if everyone agrees about the case of 'to this one and to that one', why does the משנה give that ruling in רבי עקיבא's name, as if רבנן disagree? רבא answers that רבה has the same problem, because a 'to all of you' case has no first or last person. He then reads the משנה differently. The first part is 'to all of you', and the end is a chain where each person is linked to the one before him. A ברייתא about releasing the 'middle one' supports this reading. Next, רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבא from the onion משנה, where רבי מאיר released a man from all onions. The גמרא answers that the man would have listed the onions one by one, so everyone agrees. Finally, רבינא begins a new challenge from רבי נתן, who says a vow can be partly permitted and partly forbidden; the case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why do רבנן argue if everyone agrees?
steps.stepSummary: A challenge to רבא: the end of the משנה is רבי עקיבא's view, so why would רבנן disagree if רבא says everyone agrees it is permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the משנה, where he said 'to this one and to that one', is רבי עקיבא's view. Why do the רבנן argue with him? Didn't you say that everyone agrees it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks רבא's view. רבא said everyone agrees about the 'to this one and to that one' case, yet that ruling is said in רבי עקיבא's name, which suggests others disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had said that in the 'to this one and to that one' case everyone holds the people are permitted. But a ruling is only given in one person's name when others argue. So the fact that the end of the משנה is labeled 'רבי עקיבא' seems to show that רבנן disagree, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
'To this one and to that one', naming each person separately
They argue
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: But the latter clause,
where he said, 'to this one and to that one,'
is the view of Rabbi Akiva,
why do the Rabbis disagree with him?
But you said that all agree it is permitted!
phrases.notes: 'You' means רבא, who said this earlier in the discussion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא סֵיפָא, דְּאָמַר לָזֶה וְלָזֶה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier challenge to רבא's reading of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that in the 'to this one and to that one' case everyone agrees the people are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling is given in רבי עקיבא's name, which implies a dispute with רבנן. A dispute contradicts 'everyone agrees'.

steps.title: רבא shows רבה has the same problem
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבה cannot explain the end of the משנה according to רבי עקיבא either, because in a 'to all of you' case there is no 'first' or 'last'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: And according to רבה, does the end of the משנה work out for רבי עקיבא? How would he explain it? As a case where he said 'to all of you'? Then which one is the first and which one is the last?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not answer directly. He turns the question around and shows that רבה, whose side the challenger is taking, has a problem with the same part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה speaks about releasing the 'first' person or the 'last' person. If רבה explains it as a case of 'to all of you', there is no order, so no one is 'first' or 'last'. So the challenge is not a special weakness of רבא; both sides need a new reading of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it work out well? (a question meaning it does not)
In what case does he set it up?
'To all of you', one word covering everyone together
First... last

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
And according to Rabba, for Rabbi Akiva,
does the latter clause work out well?
In what case does he establish it?
Where he said 'to all of you'?
Which one of them is the first
and which one of them is the last?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וּלְרַבָּה לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִי נִיחָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing the opposing view has the same difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's way of explaining the end of the משנה according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'to all of you' case has no order, but the משנה speaks of a first and a last person.

steps.title: A new reading: the end is about linked people
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the first part of the משנה is a case of 'to all of you', while the end is a case where he linked each person to the one before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the first part is where he said 'to all of you'. The end part is, for example, where he linked them one to another and said: 'So-and-so is like so-and-so, and so-and-so is like so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new way to read the משנה. The end part is not a simple list; each person's prohibition hangs on the one before him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the prohibitions are linked in a chain, there is a real first and last. Releasing someone releases everyone who depends on him, but not those before him. So the end of the משנה is not a plain 'to this one and to that one' case, and רבא's claim that everyone agrees about that case still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
He made them hang on one another (linked them)
So-and-so is like so-and-so

steps.confusionAlert: 'Linked' here does not just mean listing names. It means each person's prohibition depends on the one named before him, so the order matters.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading lets the first/last rulings make sense and removes the problem raised in the last two steps.

phrases.english: Rather: the first clause is where he said 'to all of you,'
and the latter clause is, for example, where he linked them to one another,
and said: 'So-and-so is like so-and-so,'
'and so-and-so is like so-and-so.'
phrases.notes: He means each new person is forbidden only because he is compared to the person before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רֵישָׁא דְּאָמַר לְכוּלְּכֶם, וְסֵיפָא, כְּגוֹן שֶׁתְּלָאָן זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in steps 1 and 2 by changing how the end of the משנה is set up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-setting the case (אוקימתא): the end of the משנה is about linked prohibitions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The end of the משנה was a plain 'to this one and to that one' or 'to all of you' case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is 'to all of you'; the end is a chain where each person is compared to the one before.

steps.title: Support from a ברייתא about the middle person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the middle person is released, those after him are permitted and those before him stay forbidden, which shows a linked chain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is exact too, as a ברייתא teaches: If the middle one was released, from him and below are permitted, and above are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבא's new reading. The ברייתא only makes sense if the people are linked in a chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the middle person's prohibition is removed, everyone named after him is freed, because their prohibitions hung on him. Those named before him did not depend on him, so they stay forbidden. This is exactly what a linked chain would produce.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is exact too (this supports the point)
The middle one
Below (named after)... above (named before)

steps.whatToRemember: In the end of the משנה, each person's prohibition is linked to the one before. Releasing someone frees everyone after him but not those before him.

phrases.english: It is also precise, as it is taught:
If the middle one was permitted,
from him and below are permitted,
phrases.notes: 'Below' means the people named after him in the list.

phrases.english: and above are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the reading given in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that the end of the משנה is about linked prohibitions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: if the middle one is released, those after him are permitted and those before him are forbidden.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה quotes the onion משנה against רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה brings the משנה about a man who vowed off onions because they are bad for the heart. In that case רבי מאיר released him from all onions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה challenged רבא: someone said, 'Onions are קונם for me, I won't taste them, because onions are bad for the heart.' People told him, 'But the כופרי onion is good for the heart!' His vow is released for כופרי onions, and not only for כופרי but for all onions. This really happened, and רבי מאיר released him for all onions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רבא by quoting a משנה. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, part of the vow fell away (the כופרי onion) because the man's reason did not apply to it. Even so, the whole vow was released and every onion became permitted. The question will be whether this result fits רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word that makes something forbidden like a קרבן
A type of onion that is good for the heart
It was released or permitted
There was an actual incident

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava raised an objection to Rava:
"Onions are konam that I will taste,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from a later משנה in this מסכת (66a).

phrases.english: because onions are bad for the heart."

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא הַכּוּפְרִי יָפֶה לַלֵּב!
phrases.english: They said to him: But isn't the kuferi onion good for the heart!
The vow is released for kuferi onions.
And not only for kuferi onions is it released,
but for all onions.
There was an incident,
and Rabbi Meir released him for all onions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's distinction is set up and supported, a new source is brought to test it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule about how the wording of a vow affects whether the rest of it stays forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: in the משנה, a vow that was partly released became fully released. The next step shows why that is hard for רבא.

steps.title: The man seems to have meant 'all onions forbidden except כופרי'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the man would have said 'all onions are forbidden and כופרי is permitted'. That wording would make רבי מאיר's full release hard to explain according to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about a man who said: 'Had I known that כופרי onions are good for the heart, I would have said: all onions are forbidden and כופרי is permitted'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes the attack sharp. It suggests the man's vow was in the 'all forbidden except X' style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the 'all are forbidden except X' wording is the case that is argued over, and the stricter side (the side רבי מאיר follows) says the rest stays forbidden. Yet here רבי מאיר himself permits all the onions. So if the משנה is about this wording, רבא's rule seems contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? It introduces a suggested reading meant to challenge
Had I known, which describes what the person would have vowed instead

phrases.english: What, is it not a case where he said:
Had I known
that the kuferi onion is good for the heart,
I would have said
"All onions are forbidden and kuferi is permitted"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted משנה becomes a challenge to רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction between the two ways of wording a vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the man meant 'all forbidden except כופרי', then according to רבא this is the argued case, and רבי מאיר's side should keep the other onions forbidden. Yet רבי מאיר releases all onions.

steps.title: No, he meant 'this onion and that onion are forbidden'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the man would have listed onions one by one ('such and such an onion are forbidden'). In that case, according to רבא, everyone agrees the whole vow is released, so רבי מאיר fits both רבי עקיבא and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a case where he says: 'Had I known that כופרי onions are good for the heart, I would have said: this onion and that onion are forbidden, and כופרי is permitted.' And רבי מאיר's ruling fits both רבי עקיבא and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by reading the משנה as the 'this one and that one' style of vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that when a person lists the items one by one, everyone agrees that releasing one part releases everything. So רבי מאיר's full release is not a special opinion here; it matches both רבי עקיבא and רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Such and such, meaning items named one by one
According to the view of
The Sages, the majority view

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a vow that lists items one by one ('this and that') is fully released by everyone once part of it falls away. The onion משנה fits that case.

phrases.english: No, it is where he says:
Had I known
that the kuferi onion is good for the heart,
I would have said:
"Such an onion and such an onion are forbidden
and kuferi is permitted."
And Rabbi Meir's ruling is according to Rabbi Akiva
and according to the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested reading from step 6 and replaces it with a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man meant 'all onions forbidden except כופרי', which would contradict רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The man meant 'this onion and that onion are forbidden', where according to רבא everyone agrees the whole vow is released.

steps.title: רבינא begins a challenge from רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבא from רבי נתן, who says some vows are partly permitted and partly forbidden. The example begins with someone who vowed off a basket of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged רבא: רבי נתן says there is a vow that is partly permitted and partly forbidden. How so? Someone vowed off the basket,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רבא. It is setting up a case that continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the focus has been on vows that become fully permitted once part is released. רבי נתן claims there is a vow where only part is released and the rest stays forbidden. That threatens רבא's position, depending on how the case is worded.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of it
How so? It introduces an example
A basket of produce

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection to Rava:
Rabbi Natan says:
There is a vow that is partly permitted
and partly forbidden.
How so? He vowed off the basket,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the onion challenge is answered, a second challenge to רבא begins from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that a partly released vow is fully released in certain wordings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: רבי נתן says some vows stay partly forbidden after part is released. The details follow in the next text.
